sources.entry: mlflow - An open-source platform for tracking experiments, managing models, and evaluating LLM apps.

summary.one_liner: MLflow is an open-source AI engineering platform for tracing, evaluating, and monitoring LLM apps and agents, plus experiment tracking, model registry, and model deployment for traditional ML.
summary.what_it_does: MLflow provides tracing for LLM applications and agents, built on OpenTelemetry, with one-line autologging for many agent frameworks and LLM providers. It offers evaluation tooling with built-in metrics and LLM judges, plus prompt versioning, lineage tracking, and automated prompt optimization. An AI Gateway gives a unified OpenAI-compatible interface to multiple LLM providers with rate limits, fallbacks, credential management, guardrails, and traffic splitting. For traditional ML and deep learning, it tracks experiments (parameters, metrics, evaluation results), manages a model registry, and supports deployment to batch and real-time scoring targets. The README lists Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, and Java support, and starts a local server with uvx mlflow server.
use_cases: debug and trace LLM app or agent behavior
evaluate LLM outputs against quality metrics
route and budget requests across LLM providers
track ML experiments and compare runs
manage a model registry and deploy models
how_to_run: Run your app code; traces appear in the MLflow UI
notable: One-line automatic tracing for more than 60 frameworks and providers
Built on OpenTelemetry and supports MCP
AI Gateway with OpenAI-compatible interface, guardrails, and A/B traffic splitting
Covers both LLM/agent work and classic ML lifecycle in one platform
Setup wizard that launches a coding agent to add tracing to an app
caveats: Some features (such as the setup wizard and certain integrations) depend on external tools like Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, or a Databricks workspace
Some deployment targets (Databricks, SageMaker, Azure ML, OpenShift AI) are managed or vendor environments the README points to rather than details here
The README links to separate docs for most features; specifics such as pricing or full integration lists are not covered in the README itself
